method_notes.note: the prior-cycle blocks and the this-cycle foreign block compare two complete trees that differ only in git HEAD content and both live at foreign paths without a .git directory. This is the faithful reproduction of the prior cycle's method.

prior_cycle_pair_asymmetric_git_presence pairs a git worktree (has .git) with a plain copy (does not). Its repaired-only set holds the cycle-caused F1 guard plus product/tests/test_ci_reality_legs.py::test_summary_and_leg_reports_are_written_for_this_run, which asserts a 40-char head sha and so needs .git. Published as a CONTROL showing the membership of these sets is a property of the measurement setup; never quote it as the repair's delta.

product/regression_scope.py --baseline-ref restores product/tests/** from a git ref by byte injection so both runs share one checkout root. It is EXACT when the repair changed only collected test code (this cycle's delta: two test modules, no non-test artifact), and it OVER-COUNTS baseline failures when the ref's tests assert against artifacts the working tree has already moved on: a same-root measurement of the 6c56332c baseline at the producer root reports more unique IDs than the 77 measured on a faithful pristine tree, the extra IDs being artifact-vs-test mismatches the method itself introduces. That figure is recorded as a method artefact and is NOT published as a baseline.

18 modules cannot be collected in this environment (missing optional dependency sentence_transformers) and are excluded from every run here, identically on both sides. Their status is UNMEASURED, not passed. The list is computed by attempting collection, never hard-coded, and is published in each measurement artifact.

every measurement reconciles passed_r - passed_b == collected_delta - net_unique_failing_delta - skipped_delta. product/regression_scope.py REFUSES to write an artifact whose arithmetic does not close, and refuses a --baseline-ref run in which no bytes were injected, which would make the comparison vacuous.
nothing in this cycle edits a frozen rubric, gate, bar, threshold or packet byte.
